summary: Deployed a 3-node RabbitMQ cluster (node1/node2/node3, AlmaLinux 9) using RabbitMQ 3.13.7 + Erlang 26 (installed from GitHub release RPM + EPEL, since RabbitMQ 4.x required Erlang 27 which wasn't available). Created a dedicated self-signed CA and issued per-node server certs (SAN = hostname+IP) plus a client cert, all under /tmp/ca on node1. Configured rabbitmq.conf on all nodes to disable plaintext AMQP (listeners.tcp = none), serve AMQP only via TLS on 5671 with ssl_options.verify = verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert = true (mutual TLS, CA-issued client certs required). Clustered all three nodes via a shared Erlang cookie and rabbitmqctl join_cluster. Enabled the management plugin (15672) on each node and restricted it via firewalld rich rules to the 10.100.214.0/24 cluster subnet only (5671 left open, 15672/4369/25672 scoped to subnet). Verified: TLS handshake succeeds with a CA-issued client cert and is rejected (fatal alerts: certificate_required / bad certificate) with no cert or an untrusted self-signed cert, on all three nodes; a full AMQPS publish/consume round-trip works via pika with mTLS; management API is reachable from cluster peers. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id + cluster/queue health baselines, rebooted node1, node2, then node3 one at a time via `systemctl reboot` (quorum preserved throughout — a replicated quorum queue's Raft leader migrated node1→node2→node3 across the sequence), polled each node until reachable again, confirmed changed boot_id and uptime≈0 as direct restart proof, and confirmed RabbitMQ rejoined the cluster (3/3 running nodes) with TLS listeners back up after each restart. Final check: the message published to the durable quorum queue before the restart sequence was still present and was successfully consumed over mTLS after all three nodes had been rebooted.
actions_performed: Installed erlang (EPEL) and rabbitmq-server 3.13.7 (GitHub release RPM) on node1, node2, node3
Set up /etc/hosts and cluster SSH keys on all nodes
Generated a dedicated CA and per-node TLS server certs + a client cert + an untrusted cert for negative testing on node1, distributed to node2/node3 via scp
Configured rabbitmq.conf: TLS-only AMQP listener (5671) with verify_peer + fail_if_no_peer_cert, management on 15672, classic_config cluster peer discovery, pause_minority partition handling
Shared Erlang cookie across all 3 nodes
Opened firewalld rules: 5671 open globally, 4369/25672/15672 restricted to 10.100.214.0/24 cluster subnet
Joined node2 and node3 to node1's cluster via rabbitmqctl join_cluster after fixing firewall-blocked Erlang distribution
Created admin user, deleted default guest user
Verified mTLS enforcement (accept valid CA cert, reject no-cert and untrusted-cert) via openssl s_client and RabbitMQ logs on all 3 nodes
Verified end-to-end AMQPS publish/consume with pika using CA-issued client cert
Verified management API reachable cluster-internally and firewall-restricted externally via nft ruleset inspection
Created a durable quorum queue replicated across all 3 nodes with a persistent test message

Executed mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id + health baseline, restarted node1, node2, node3 sequentially via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id change + uptime reset, confirmed RabbitMQ/cluster/TLS recovery and quorum queue leader failover after each restart
Final verification: consumed the pre-restart message over mTLS after all restarts, confirming data durability

evidence.summary: cluster_status shows all 3 nodes (rabbit@node1/2/3) as Disk Nodes and Running Nodes

evidence.requirement: AMQP over TLS using CA created for this cluster
evidence.summary: CA generated on node1, node certs signed and verified against it, listeners.tcp=none + listeners.ssl.default=5671 configured, and a full pika AMQPS publish/consume succeeded using the CA-issued client cert

evidence.requirement: Accept only client connections presenting a CA-issued certificate
evidence.summary: Valid client cert handshake succeeds (Verify return code 0); no-cert and untrusted-cert attempts are rejected with fatal TLS alerts (certificate_required / bad certificate) confirmed via openssl s_client, server logs on node1/2/3, and a pika-level rejection

evidence.requirement: Management interface reachable only within the cluster
evidence.summary: nft ruleset shows port 15672 accept rule scoped to source 10.100.214.0/24 only (no broader allow), and management API confirmed reachable from a cluster peer (node1->node2)
Pre-restart boot_id captured plus active rabbitmq-server and full 3-node cluster_status

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returns before disconnect, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot command acked and returned before disconnect; subsequent polls show connection reset/timeout then a new boot_id (67f3a44b->6ed3136f) with uptime 0; rabbitmq-server became active again and cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running; TLS handshake verified working post-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id captured, reboot acked, connection reset observed, new boot_id (1b0321bf->9f03f317) with uptime 0 confirmed, rabbitmq-server active with all 3 nodes running, TLS verified, and quorum queue data confirmed present via node1

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id captured, reboot acked, connection reset/timeout observed, new boot_id (c207ab79->f20a47d2) with uptime 0 confirmed, rabbitmq-server active, cluster_status shows all 3 nodes running, TLS verified

evidence.requirement: Data/cluster health and quorum preserved across full restart sequence
evidence.summary: Durable quorum queue created and published to before restarts; after all 3 sequential node restarts the queue still shows the message (messages:1, all 3 members online) and the original message body was successfully consumed over mTLS, proving no data loss and full cluster/quorum recovery
